items.title: Section: When Even the Finest Flowers Vanish From the World

items.zh: 若器世間農作、行船、世俗事業不甚滋息，殊少便宜，多不諧偶，饒諸怖畏恐懼因緣。如是一切，是妄語增上果。若器世間其地處所，丘坑間隔，險阻難行，饒諸怖畏恐懼因緣。如是一切，是離間語增上果。若器世間其地處所，多諸株杌、荊棘、毒刺、瓦石、沙礫，枯槁無潤，無有池沼，河泉乾竭，土田鹹鹵，丘陵坑險，饒諸怖畏恐懼因緣。如是一切，是麁惡語增上果。若器世間所有果樹果無的當，非時結實，時不結實，生而似熟，根不堅牢，勢不久停，園林池沼多不可樂，饒諸怖畏恐懼因緣。如是一切，是綺語增上果。若器世間一切盛事，年時日夜月半月等漸漸衰微，所有氣味唯減不增。如是一切，是貪欲增上果。若器世間多諸疫癘、災橫、擾惱、怨敵、驚怖、師子、虎狼、雜惡禽獸、蟒蛇、蝮蝎、蚰蜒、百足、魍魎、藥叉、諸惡賊等。如是一切，是瞋恚增上果。若器世間所有第一勝妙華果悉皆隱沒，諸不淨物乍似清淨，諸苦惱物乍似安樂，非安居所、非救護所、非歸依所。如是一切，是邪見增上果。
items.en: If, in the material world, farming, seafaring, and worldly enterprise do not flourish, bring little advantage, and rarely succeed, thick with occasions of fear and dread — all of this is the dominant fruit of false speech. If, in the material world, hills and ravines lie between places, the terrain treacherous and hard to traverse, thick with fear and dread — all of this is the dominant fruit of divisive speech. If, in the material world, there are many bare stumps, thorns, poisonous brambles, tiles, gravel, and sand, dry and unnourished, without ponds, rivers and springs run dry, the soil salty, hills and gorges dangerous, thick with fear and dread — all of this is the dominant fruit of harsh speech. If, in the material world, fruit trees bear out of season or fail to bear, or bear what looks ripe but is not, rooted shallowly and short-lived, gardens and pools unpleasant, thick with fear and dread — all of this is the dominant fruit of idle chatter. If, in the material world, every flourishing thing gradually diminishes year by year, day by day, and every flavour only fades and never grows — all of this is the dominant fruit of covetousness. If, in the material world, there is much plague, calamity, affliction, hostility, and terror, lions, tigers, wolves, and every fierce beast, serpents, venomous creatures, malevolent spirits, and violent bandits — all of this is the dominant fruit of hatred. If, in the material world, the finest flowers and fruits all vanish, impure things appear pure, and wretched things appear pleasant, offering no dwelling, no protection, and no refuge — all of this is the dominant fruit of wrong view.

items.title: Section: For Meat, For Robbery, For a False Friend's Sacrifice

items.zh: 復次，如世尊言：殺有三種。謂貪瞋癡之所生起，乃至邪見亦復如是。此差別義，云何應知？若為血肉等，殺害眾生。或作是心：殺害彼已，當奪財物。或受他雇、或為報恩、或友所攝、或希為友、或為衣食，奉主教命而行殺害。或有謂彼能為衰損，或有謂彼能障財利，而行殺害。如利衰，毀譽、稱譏、苦樂，隨其所應，當知亦爾。如是一切，名貪所生殺生業道。復次，若謂彼於己樂為無義，而行殺害。或念彼於己曾為無義，或恐彼於己當為無義，或見彼於己正為無義，而行殺害；廣說乃至於九惱事，皆如是知。如是一切，名瞋所生殺生業道。復次，若計為法而行殺害，謂己是餘眾生善友，彼因我殺，身壞命終當生天上。如是殺害，從癡所生。
items.en: Moreover, as the Blessed One said: killing is of three kinds, arising from greed, hatred, and delusion, and so too even with wrong view. How should this distinction be understood? If killing beings for flesh and blood; or forming the thought, having killed them, I shall then take their wealth; or hired by another, or repaying kindness, or drawn by a friend, or hoping to gain friendship, or for food and clothing, obeying a master's command and carrying out killing; or holding that another is capable of causing decline, or capable of obstructing profit, and carrying out killing; as with gain and loss, so too with disrepute and repute, praise and blame, pleasure and pain, accordingly — all of this is called killing generated by greed. Moreover, if holding that another delights in doing oneself harm, and carrying out killing on this basis, and so on at length through the nine grounds of ill will, all should be understood likewise — all of this is called killing generated by hatred. Moreover, if computing killing as righteous conduct, thinking, I am this being's good friend, and because of my killing, their body destroyed and life ended, they will be reborn in the heavens — such killing arises from delusion.

items.title: Section: Abandoning the Dying, and Theft's Own Three Roots

items.zh: 或作是心：為尊長故，法應殺害。或作是心：諸有誹毀天梵世主，罵婆羅門，法應殺害。如是心殺，從癡所生。或計殺生作及增長無異熟果，為他開演勸行殺業，彼由勸故，遂行殺事。時彼勸者所得殺罪，從癡所生。此後所說從癡所生殺業道理，諸餘業道乃至邪見，當知亦爾。或有妄計以其父母親愛眷屬擲置火中，斷食、投巖、棄於曠野，是真正法。如是一切，名癡所生殺生業道。復次，若於他財食饕餮而取。是不與取，貪欲所生。
items.en: Or thinking, for the sake of an elder, this killing should be done by righteous law; or thinking, those who slander the heavens, Brahmā, or the lord of the world, or curse brahmins, should by righteous law be killed. Such killing arises from delusion. Or computing that killing, whether committed or increased, has no ripening result, and openly teaching and urging another to carry out killing, so that they, persuaded, go on to kill — the one who so persuaded them incurs the offence of killing, arising from delusion. Or falsely computing that placing one's own parents or beloved family into fire, starving them, casting them from a cliff, or abandoning them in the wilderness is itself genuinely righteous conduct. All of this is called killing generated by delusion. Moreover, gluttonously taking another's wealth or food is taking what is not given, generated by greed.

items.title: Section: Burning a Village Out of Pure Spite

items.zh: 或受他雇而行劫盜，或恩所攝、或祈後恩、或為衣食奉主教命、或為稱譽、或為安樂而行劫盜。如是一切不與取業，皆貪所生。復次，若作是思：彼於我所樂行無義，廣說乃至九惱害事增上力故，而行劫盜。不必貪著彼所有財，不必希求諸餘財物。是不與取，瞋恚所生。或憎他故，焚燒聚落舍宅財物珍玩資具，當知彼觸瞋恚所生，盜相似罪，或更增強。或憎彼故，令他劫奪，破散彼財。他受教命依行事時，彼能教者不與取罪，從瞋恚生。復次，若作是心：為尊長故而行劫盜，是為正法。名癡所生不與取罪。或作是心：若有誹毀天梵世主，罵婆羅門，法應奪彼所有財物。此不與取亦從癡生。或作是心：若為祠祀、為祠祀支、為祠祀具，法應劫盜。是不與取亦從癡生。
items.en: Or committing theft for hire, out of gratitude, hoping for future kindness, for food and clothing under a master's command, for praise, or for comfort — all such taking of what is not given arises from greed. Moreover, thinking, this one delights in doing me harm, and so on through the nine grounds of ill will, committing theft without craving the wealth itself or seeking any other gain — this is taking what is not given, generated by hatred. Or, out of hatred, burning down a village's homes, possessions, and treasures — this should be known as a crime resembling theft generated by hatred, or graver still. Or, out of hatred, commanding another to plunder and scatter another's wealth — the one who gives such a command incurs the offence of taking what is not given, arising from hatred. Moreover, thinking, for the sake of an elder this theft is righteous conduct — this is taking what is not given, generated by delusion. Or thinking, one who slanders the heavens, Brahmā, or brahmins should by righteous law have their wealth seized — this too arises from delusion. Or thinking, for the sake of sacrifice, its accessories, or its implements, this theft is righteous — this too arises from delusion.

items.zh: 復次，若有見聞不應行事，便不如理分別取相，遂貪欲纏之所纏縛而行非法，名貪所生欲邪行罪。或受他雇竊行媒嫁，由此方便行所不行，彼便獲得貪欲所生欲邪行罪。

blocks.text: How each wrong deed shapes the outer world, and how each arises from greed, hatred, or delusion.

Master Cháng Bǎi: having obstructed others' harmony, one receives a world without ease. Harsh words give thorny, parched ground; idle chatter gives fruit that looks ripe but cannot be eaten. Under wrong view, every fine thing declines day by day. The world corresponds to the human mind: if people practise the ten good deeds, the world around them is fine.
Master Cháng Bǎi: killing for meat or for gain is from greed; killing for elders, wrong faith, or race is joined with delusion: one thinks oneself a friend whose killing sends others to heaven.

Master Cháng Bǎi: some falsely hold that the dying should be put into fire; the right attitude is care to the last moment. Theft from greed is taking the coveted thing greedily, as if wolfing it down.

Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not crave the wealth; it is pure revenge. Burning a village out of spite resembles robbery, or is graver, since it ruins the other completely. (Untranslated, 0634b17: misconduct born of greed, and arranging another's illicit union for hire.)
"The world corresponds to the human mind." This is not mysticism in the treatise; it is a description of how shared actions shape shared conditions.

quiz.q: What are the dominant fruits of false and divisive speech?
options: enterprises fail and rarely succeed; hills and ravines, hard to traverse
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: enterprises do not grow, go badly, and fail to pair well; having obstructed others' harmony, one receives an environment without ease of going in and out. The fruit mirrors the deed, division giving a divided landscape.

quiz.q: What are the dominant fruits of harsh speech and idle chatter?
options: plague and beasts; gradual decline, unrelated to land or fruit trees
stumps, thorns, gravel, parched salty soil; fruit out of season, seeming ripe
quiz.why: Harsh words give thorny, parched ground; idle chatter gives fruit that looks ripe but cannot be eaten. Master Cháng Bǎi describes such unripe fruit that seems ripe yet is inedible, a fit image for empty speech. The English "bear what looks ripe but is not" is close.

quiz.q: What are the dominant fruits of covetousness, malice, and wrong view?
options: flourishing declining; plague and beasts; finest fruits vanishing, impure seeming pure
scarce fruit; rough land; failed work
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: every fine and flourishing thing declines day by day; impure things seem pure, and painful things seem pleasant. So wrong view distorts even the appearance of the world, matching its own nature. The English "hatred" here is 瞋恚 again, elsewhere "malice."

quiz.q: How do the world's condition and the human mind relate?
options: the world changes with the human mind; ten wholesome deeds make it fine
the world is matter independent of mind, the fruits being figures of speech, environmental problems having only physical causes
only a buddha can change it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the change and decay of the material world corresponds to the human mind; if people practice the ten wholesome deeds, the world around them is fine and excellent. A good text for discussing ethics and environment with Western readers.

quiz.q: Which deeds' dominant fruits include "thick with fear and dread"?
options: the four speech deeds: false, divisive, harsh, idle
quiz.why: The refrain closes each of the four speech paths' fruits in the treatise, and it does not appear for bodily or mental paths. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the first as things going badly. The English "thick with fear and dread" reproduces the refrain.

quiz.q: What examples of killing born of greed are given?
options: for flesh, wealth, hire, gratitude, friends, livelihood, gain and loss
revenge, removing foes, and venting anger, the nine grounds also being greed, unrelated to hatred
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: killing and then seizing wealth is a second case; others are for another's sake; and killing one who blocks one's profit is for gain or loss. So the poison classifies the motive, not the act. The English covers these.

quiz.q: The English has "another has done oneself no benefit." What is wrong with its direction?
options: no problem: 無義 means no benefit, disappointment causing anger, §§12–13 being the same, as the lecture says
the Chinese says the other delights in doing me harm; the English says merely no benefit, dropping 樂
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi at §12 reads the same phrase as the other delighting in doing all manner of harmful things to oneself; at §10 he sums up the nine grounds of ill will. As 瞋 needs an offence, the English "no benefit" is too weak, and 樂 is dropped in all three places.

quiz.q: What are examples of killing born of delusion?
options: for flesh, hire, or livelihood, all being ignorant of causality, greed and delusion being one class
killing as Dharma for another's heaven; for elders; slanderers; urging killing; casting kin in fire
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one thinks oneself a good friend whose killing lets others go to heaven; killing for elders, wrong faith, or race is joined with delusion. Common to these is the belief that the act is right. The English "computing killing as righteous conduct" fits.

quiz.q: The English has "whether committed or repeated." What is the problem, and who incurs the offence?
options: 作及增長 is §7's technical pair, to be "committed" and "increased"; the one urging incurs it
no problem: 增長 means repeating, and only the one who kills incurs guilt
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: thinking killing brings no ripening, one tells others it is faultless and teaches them to kill; the offence of killing by urging is the third case of delusion. "Repeated" loses the link to §7's pair committed and increased. The persuader incurs the offence.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi assess casting kin into fire or abandoning them as Dharma?
options: a local custom, faultless with family consent, to be respected, the treatise only recording it
a false clinging; one must care for kin to the last, not abandoning them while life remains
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: some falsely hold that parents and loved ones should be put into fire; the right attitude is care to the last moment, not abandoning kin before their life is over. The treatise classes such acts as killing born of delusion.

quiz.q: What are examples of theft born of greed?
options: burning in revenge, satisfaction being greed's mark
gluttonous taking; for hire, gratitude, a master, praise, or comfort
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: taking the coveted thing greedily, as if wolfing it down, is the first case. The treatise repeats for theft the same pattern as killing: for hire, gratitude, or livelihood. The English "gluttonously taking" keeps 饕餮.

quiz.q: What marks theft born of hatred?
options: wealth must be wanted, theft being for wealth, hatred merely accompanying greed, the two being inseparable
no craving for the wealth, purely revenge, plundering through ill will
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not crave the wealth, nor seek other wealth; it is purely revenge. So theft can arise from hatred alone. The English "without craving the wealth itself or seeking any other gain" follows the Chinese.

quiz.q: What offence does burning a village out of hatred incur?
options: a crime resembling theft born of hatred, or graver still
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is a crime resembling robbery born of hatred, or graver than robbery, since it ruins the other completely. Thus harm can outweigh gain as a measure. The English "or graver still" matches.

quiz.q: The English has "the one who gives such a command incurs the offence." What is left out?
options: nothing: guilt arises on commanding, whether or not it is done, 依行事時 being an aside
the condition: only when the other acts on it; the English implies guilt on commanding
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the one who instructs incurs a theft offence born of hatred. The treatise specifies the time: when the other accepts and acts. §11's English keeps this condition, and here it is dropped, along with the parallel in §13.
